subject: Bootstrapped cohort discount — slab proposal and terms
messages:
From: Sofia Martinez <sofia@lumenpath.co>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-04-28T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Intro pricing ask — LumenPath cohort (introductory proposal)

Hi Aisha,

Quick intro — I'm Sofia (program director for LumenPath Accelerator). We're kicking off a new spring cohort (20 teams, mostly bootstrap or pre-seed) and looking to negotiate a simple consumption discount package to include in our partner benefits. The ask from the founders is: a predictable, easy-to-communicate "slab" subsidy so they can plan usage during the 12-week program.

High level:
- Cohort size: ~20 startups, 2 average seats each
- Expected avg usage: 30M tokens/month per startup (bursty) with spikes during demo week
- Need a short-term promo for 3 months + an onboarding playbook

We're not looking for a long-term enterprise contract — this is a marketing/enablement play. That said, the founders need a clear per-team floor/ceiling they can expect. Could Redwood do a slab discount model (e.g., first N tokens at X% off, then tiered billing) or a fixed grant + discounted overage?

I've attached a simple spreadsheet with cohort demographics and approximate usage patterns (accelerator_terms.xlsx). Can we set up the smallest internal review and a proposal you could send to the partners by next week?

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call.

Sofia Martinez
Program Director, LumenPath Accelerator
sofia@lumenpath.co

Attachment: accelerator_terms.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Cc: Sofia Martinez <sofia@lumenpath.co>
Date: 2028-04-29T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Intro pricing ask — LumenPath cohort (introductory proposal)

Team — forwarding LumenPath's ask. Their cohort is small but high-touch; they want something that founders can easily understand and sell in recruitment materials. Sofia's asked for a slab or grant + discounted overage for a 3 month window.

Notes / questions I have:
- We should avoid a bespoke credit pool that requires manual reconciliation unless we can template it.
- Prefer a program that maps to our billing (per-token + discounted percentage) so finance doesn't have a dozen special SKUs.
- Can we propose a 3-month promotional "Starter Slab": first 500k tokens per team/month at 80% discount, next tier up to 2M at 50% discount, overage at 20% discount? Or an alternate: $4k fixed grant per team + 30% off overage.

Marissa — real cost impact on us (and any SOW/legal issues) if we do percent discounts vs fixed grants?
Ben — will this be a marketing co-op (we give discounts in exchange for PR/partner placement) or do we need a revenue-recognition-friendly structure?
Karthik — compliance or ATL concerns if we enable hardware credits or reserved capacity carveouts for certain startups?

I'd like to get a single-sheet proposal back to Sofia with 2 options (slab vs grant) and a short list of operational caveats. I can draft the outbound if you share numbers.

Thanks,
Aisha
Senior Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Cc: Sofia Martinez <sofia@lumenpath.co>
Date: 2028-04-30T14:35:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Intro pricing ask — LumenPath cohort (introductory proposal)

Aisha — quick thoughts from deal ops / partner program POV.

Slab (per-team): pros = simple for founders to understand, easy to display as "included benefits" on their program page. Cons = heavy to reconcile if founders vary widely in consumption (we'll see a lot of zero-to-spike patterns).

Grant + overage: pros = predictable committed cost for us, aligns with marketing goals if we make grant conditional on partner-facing wins (e.g., demo participation). Cons = requires per-team grant issuance and a light SOW.

Operational recommendations:
- Create a templated SOW (one-page) with standard terms: 3-month window, per-team grant amount, overage discount percentage, attribution/PR obligations, and a 30-day usage reporting cadence. I can draft SOW verbiage — uploading a redline-ready PDF: LumenPath_SOW_v1.pdf.
- For billing, prefer grant issuance as account credits (easier for finance) rather than percent-off coupons. Finance can allocate a partner budget and we invoice LumenPath monthly for net consumption.
- If they want reserved hardware credits, we should limit that to Dedicated customers only — specify it as an addendum.

I'll attach a proposed slab table for their cohort with per-team bands (proposed_slab_table.csv). If we go with grant + overage, I'd suggest $3,500 grant / team for 3 months + 30% overage discount. That balances marketing optics and cost.

Marissa
Head of Partner Programs, Redwood Inference

Attachments: LumenPath_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW draft), proposed_slab_table.csv (CSV)

From: Sofia Martinez <sofia@lumenpath.co>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-05-01T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Intro pricing ask — Introductory proposal

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. LumenPath's priorities: clarity for founders and a low-friction onboarding experience. A few clarifying points from our side: 

- Grant vs slab: founders prefer messaging that shows a predictable grant ("your cohort includes $X credits") — that's easy to understand.
- Hardware carveouts: we have a small set of teams using edge devices; we can accept a Dedicated addendum if that's surfaced as optional.
- Billing/finance: we don't expect to pre-pay for cohort usage; we can cover net consumption monthly if Redwood invoices LumenPath for partner-covered consumption.

Action items for Redwood:
1) If you can send a one-pager SOW + a per-team grant number we can present to our partners by EOD Thursday, that's perfect.
2) Include a short onboarding runbook so founders know how to redeem credits and where support lives (a sample runbook would do).

I'll attach a brief usage template we use internally (usage_runbook.xlsx) to show typical onboarding steps. Once we have the SOW and numbers we'll route through our legal and sign.

Sofia

Attachment: usage_runbook.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.inference>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia@lumenpath.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-05-03T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Intro pricing ask — Bootstrapped cohort discount — slab proposal and terms

Sofia — thanks for the quick turnaround and the runbook. We're good to propose the grant approach as the primary option with a slab table as an alternate. Final proposal below for LumenPath's review: 

Option A (preferred): Per-team grant = $3,250 (applied as account credit) for 3 months + 30% overage discount on billable tokens. Conditions: credit expires at end of month 3; founders must opt into a one-page attribution/PR ask; no reserved hardware credits included (Dedicated carveout possible via addendum).

Option B (alternative): Starter Slab — first 400k tokens/month per team at 75% discount; next up to 1.5M at 45% discount; overage at 25% discount. This is more operationally complex for finance but workable for a cohort-wide offer.

We will:
- Send a templated SOW for signature (DocuSign link will follow)
- Provide a short onboarding runbook and a redemption flow for founders (we'll adapt your usage_runbook.xlsx)
- Redwood partner ops will invoice LumenPath monthly for the net usage after credits are applied (Net 30)

If this looks good, Marissa will send the SOW and I'll push the DocuSign. Ben — please confirm billing flow and revenue recognition. Karthik — flag any compliance/ATL items.

Looking forward — I can have the SOW in draft by EOD.

Best,
Aisha
Senior Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
